nodes.name: Deligne-Langlands-Lusztig classification
nodes.statement: Kazhdan and Lusztig \cite{KaLu} and Ginzburg \cite{CG} gave a classification and construction of irreducible representations of the affine Hecke algebra $H_{q,k}$ when $k$ is the complex number field and $q$ is not a root of unity, which is known as the Deligne-Langlands-Lusztig classification.
nodes.statement_short: Kazhdan-Lusztig and Ginzburg classify the irreducible representations of the affine Hecke algebra $H_{q,k}$ over $\mathbb{C}$ for $q$ not a root of unity.
assumptions: $k$ is the complex number field and $q$ is not a root of unity
conclusions: a classification and construction of irreducible representations of the affine Hecke algebra $H_{q,k}$

nodes.name: Lascoux-Leclerc-Thibon conjecture
nodes.statement: Lascoux, Leclerc, and Thibon \cite{LLT} suggested the conjecture that the decomposition numbers can be computed using the canonical bases of quantum groups of affine type $A.$
nodes.statement_short: Decomposition numbers of the type-$A$ Iwahori-Hecke algebra at an $e$th root of unity should be computable from canonical bases of affine type $A$ quantum groups.
assumptions: the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of type $A$ at an $e$th root of unity over $\mathbb{C}$
conclusions: the decomposition numbers can be computed using the canonical bases of quantum groups of affine type $A.$

nodes.name: Ariki's theorem
nodes.statement: Ariki \cite{Ari} proved this conjecture by establishing a connection between the representation theory of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and the canonical bases of integrable highest weight modules over $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{e}(\mathbb{C}).$
nodes.statement_short: Ariki proves the LLT conjecture by linking cyclotomic Hecke algebra representations to canonical bases of integrable highest weight $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_e$-modules.
assumptions: using the geometric results of Kazhdan-Lusztig and Ginzburg
conclusions: a connection between the representation theory of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and the canonical bases of integrable highest weight modules over $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{e}(\mathbb{C})

nodes.name: Cyclotomic categorification conjecture
nodes.statement: Khovanov and Lauda \cite{KhLa1} suggested the cyclotomic categorification conjecture, which was proved by Brundan and Kleshchev \cite{BK2} for type $A_{\infty}$ and $A_{n}^{(1)}$ using the isomorphism between the cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras of type $A$ and the cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type $A$ which was established in \cite{BK1}, and proved by Kang and Kashiwara \cite{KK} for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras.
nodes.statement_short: Khovanov-Lauda's cyclotomic categorification conjecture, proved in type $A$ by Brundan-Kleshchev and in general by Kang-Kashiwara.
nodes.origin_citation: Khovanov & Lauda; Brundan & Kleshchev; Kang & Kashiwara
assumptions: the isomorphism between the cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras of type $A$ and the cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type $A$
conclusions: proved by Kang and Kashiwara \cite{KK} for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras

nodes.name: Brundan and Kleshchev's isomorphism theorem
nodes.statement: Brundan and Kleshchev's isomorphism theorem was independently proved by Rouquier [Rou1, Corollaries 3.17 and 3.20], which allows us to construct an explicit $\mathbb{Z}$-grading on the cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type $A$ and study their graded representation theory \cite{BK2}.
nodes.statement_short: The BK isomorphism (also proved by Rouquier) yields an explicit $\mathbb{Z}$-grading on type-$A$ cyclotomic Hecke algebras.
conclusions: allows us to construct an explicit $\mathbb{Z}$-grading on the cyclotomic Hecke algebras of type $A$

nodes.name: Rouquier's categorical equivalence theorem
nodes.statement: Rouquier \cite{Rou1} also proved that certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Rouquier: a module category of an (degenerate) affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to a counterpart category of a quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$.
assumptions: certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra
conclusions: is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$

nodes.name: Rostam's theorem
nodes.statement: Rostam \cite{Ro} has shown that cyclotomic Yokonuma-Hecke algebras are particular cases of cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras, generalizing the results of Brundan and Kleshchev.
nodes.statement_short: Rostam: cyclotomic Yokonuma-Hecke algebras are special cases of cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras.
conclusions: are particular cases of cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras

nodes.name: Yokonuma-Hecke algebra $Y_{r,n}(q)$
nodes.statement: Yokonuma-Hecke algebras were introduced by Yokonuma \cite{Yo} as a centralizer algebra associated to the permutation representation of a finite Chevalley group $G$ with respect to a maximal unipotent subgroup of $G$. The Yokonuma-Hecke algebra $Y_{r,n}(q)$ (of type $A$) is a quotient of the group algebra of the modular framed braid group $(\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\wr B_{n},$ where $B_{n}$ is the braid group on $n$ strands (of type $A$).
nodes.statement_short: $Y_{r,n}(q)$ is a quotient of the group algebra of the modular framed braid group $(\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\wr B_{n}$.
nodes.genus: a quotient of the group algebra of the modular framed braid group $(\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\wr B_{n},$
differentia: where $B_{n}$ is the braid group on $n$ strands (of type $A$)

nodes.name: Standing setup: $r,n$, the field $k$, $\zeta$, $p$, $q$ and $e$
nodes.statement: Let $r, n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1},$ and let $k$ be a field which contains a primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta.$ Let $p$ be the characteristic of $k$ and consider an element $q\in k^{*}.$ We denote by $e$ the smallest integer such that $1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0$, and set $e:=\infty$ if no such integer exists.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $r,n\ge 1$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$ containing a primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta$, an element $q\in k^{*}$, and let $e$ be the quantum characteristic.

nodes.name: The quiver $I_{q}$
nodes.statement: Assume first that $q=1.$ Given a subset $I$ of $k,$ we denote by $I_{1}$ the quiver with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow i+1$ whenever $i, i+1\in I.$ Assume now that $q\neq 1.$ Given a subset $I$ of $k^{*},$ we denote by $I_{q}$ the quiver with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow qi$ whenever $i, qi\in I.$
nodes.statement_short: $I_q$ is the quiver on a subset $I\subseteq k^{*}$ with an arrow $i\to qi$ (resp. $i\to i+1$ when $q=1$).
nodes.genus: the quiver with set of vertices $I$
differentia: with an arrow $i\rightarrow i+1$ whenever $i, i+1\in I

nodes.name: Type of the connected quiver $I_{q}$
nodes.statement: Assume that $I_{q}$ is connected. Note that when $q=1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< p$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $p=0;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $p=0;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{p-1}$ if $|I|=p> 0.$ When $q\neq 1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< e$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $e=\infty;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $e=\infty;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{e-1}$ if $|I|=e> 0.$
nodes.statement_short: A connected $I_q$ is of type $A_\ell$, $A_\infty$ or $\widetilde{A}_{e-1}$ according to $|I|$ and $p$ (resp. $e$).
conclusions: $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< p$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $p=0;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $p=0;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{p-1}$ if $|I|=p> 0.$
$I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< e$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $e=\infty;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $e=\infty;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{e-1}$ if $|I|=e> 0.$

nodes.statement: The affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},\ldots,g_{n-1},X_{1}^{\pm1},$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations: \begin{align} g_ig_j&=g_jg_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;}\\[0.1em] g_ig_{i+1}g_i&=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;}\\[0.1em] t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.1em] g_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}g_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.1em] t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.2em] g_{i}^{2}&=q+(q-1)e_{i}g_{i} \qquad \hspace{0.48cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align} where $s_{i}$ is the transposition $(i,i+1)$, and for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$, $$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s},$$ together with the following relations concerning the generators $X_{1}^{\pm1}$: \begin{align} X_{1}X_{1}^{-1}&=X_{1}^{-1}X_{1}=1;\\[0.1em] g_{1}X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}g_{1};\\[0.1em] g_{i}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $i=2,\ldots,n-1$;}\\[0.1em] t_{j}X_{1}&=X_{1}t_{j} \qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$ is the $\mathcal{R}$-algebra on $t_i$, $g_i$, $X_1^{\pm1}$ with braid, framing and quadratic relations $g_i^2=q+(q-1)e_ig_i$ plus the affine relations for $X_1$.

nodes.name: Degenerate affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$ (Definition 4.1)
nodes.statement: The degenerate affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},f_{1},\ldots,f_{n-1},y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations: \begin{align} f_if_j&=f_jf_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;}\\[0.1em] f_if_{i+1}f_i&=f_{i+1}f_if_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;}\\[0.1em] t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.1em] f_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}f_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.1em] t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;}\\[0.2em] f_{i}^{2}&=1 \qquad \hspace{2.71cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align} together with the following relations concerning the generators $y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$: \begin{align} y_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}y_{i};\\[0.1em] f_{i}y_{i+1}&=y_{i}f_{i}+e_{i};\\[0.1em] f_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}f_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $j\neq i, i+1$;}\\[0.1em] t_{j}y_{i}&=y_{i}t_{j} \hspace{0.07cm}\qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $i, j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align} where for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$, $$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s}.
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$ is the $\mathcal{R}$-algebra on $t_i$, $f_i$ with $f_i^2=1$, and polynomial generators $y_i$ satisfying $f_iy_{i+1}=y_if_i+e_i$.

nodes.name: The category $\bar{\mathcal{C}}_{K}$
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}^{k}(1)=k\otimes_{\mathcal{R}}\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$ and let $M$ be a $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}^{k}(1)$-module. Given $\alpha=(\nu, j)\in K^{n},$ we denote by $M_{\alpha}$ the subspace of $M$ on which $y_{a}-\nu_{a}$ acts locally nilpotently for $1\leq a\leq n,$ and simultaneously, $t_{a}-\zeta^{j_{a}}$ acts as zero for $1\leq a\leq n.$ Let $\bar{\mathcal{C}}_{K}$ be the category of finitely generated $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}^{k}(1)$-modules $M$ such that $M=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in K^{n}}M_{\alpha}.$
nodes.statement_short: Degenerate analogue of $\mathcal{C}_K$: finitely generated $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}^{k}(1)$-modules that split into weight spaces for the $y_a$ and $t_a$.

nodes.name: Weight space $M(\nu, j)$ in the degenerate case
nodes.statement: Given an object $M\in \bar{\mathcal{C}}_{K}$, we can write $M$ as the direct sum of its weight spaces (simultaneous generalized eigenspaces): \begin{equation} M(\nu, j)=\{v\in M\:|\:(y_{a}-\nu_{a})^{N}v=(t_{a}-\zeta^{j_{a}})v=0\text{ for all }1\leq a\leq n\text{ and }N\gg 0\}.
